title: Strict pullbacks of quasicategorical isofibrations compute categorical pullbacks
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functor categories, cores, spaces and degreewise simplicial pullbacks as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and isofibrations as defined in [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation]. Fix a universe of small simplicial sets and a larger universe for $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$, the infinity category of small quasicategories and functors, whose mapping space from $Q$ to $E$ is $\operatorname{Fun}(Q,E)^\simeq$. Let $E,B,T$ be small quasicategories, $p:E\to B$ an isofibration, and $g:T\to B$ any functor. The degreewise simplicial pullback $D=T\times_B E$ is a quasicategory. Its projection square is a pullback square in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$. Explicitly, for every small quasicategory $Q$, the canonical comparison
$$\operatorname{Fun}(Q,D)^\simeq\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(Q,T)^\simeq\mathop{\times}^{h}_{\operatorname{Fun}(Q,B)^\simeq}\operatorname{Fun}(Q,E)^\simeq$$
is an equivalence of spaces. Here $A\times_C^h A'$ for maps of Kan complexes means the path-space pullback $A\times_{C,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,C)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,C}A'$, and the comparison uses the constant path between the two equal composites. No fibration hypothesis on $g$ and no nonemptiness hypothesis on $D$ is imposed.

source.place: Corollary 4.5.3.28 (Kerodon Tag 033R), with the core-functor characterization of categorical pullbacks in Proposition 4.5.3.15; equivalently Corollary 4.5.3.29. Kerodon tags, not Stacks tags: no Stacks tag states this quasicategorical theorem. Read online 2026-10-17; WANTED: archived source.

proof.text: The strict pullback $D=T\times_B E$ is a quasicategory by a direct inner-horn lifting argument. Given $\Lambda_i^n\to D$, first project to $T$ and choose a filler $t:\Delta^n\to T$, using that $T$ is a quasicategory. The $E$ coordinate of the horn and $g\circ t$ form a lifting problem against $p$. Since $p$ is an inner fibration, choose a lift $e:\Delta^n\to E$ with $p\circ e=g\circ t$. The pair $(t,e)$ is the required filler in $D$. No choices are needed when there is no horn map, so the argument allows $D=\varnothing$.

source.place: Corollary 4.4.3.19, proof of (1); inner-horn argument written out.

proof.text: Fix a small quasicategory $Q$. Put $F=\operatorname{Fun}(Q,T)$, $G=\operatorname{Fun}(Q,B)$, $H=\operatorname{Fun}(Q,E)$ and $J=\operatorname{Fun}(Q,D)$. Apply the exponential-corner statement with $A=\varnothing$ and $B=Q$ to $p$, and also to the identity isofibrations of $T$ and $D$. The identity of a quasicategory is an isofibration: its inner-horn and equivalence-edge lifting problems are filled by the given bottom simplex or edge itself. Here $\operatorname{Fun}(\varnothing,-)=\Delta^0$, so the exponential-corner statement gives that $F,G,H,J$ are quasicategories and $p_Q:H\to G$ is an isofibration. In degree $n$, a map $Q\times\Delta^n\to D$ is exactly a pair of maps to $T,E$ with equal composites to $B$. This identifies $J$ with $F\times_G H$ as simplicial sets, compatibly with both projections and all operators.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.5.1 with empty subcomplex, and the degreewise internal-Hom definition.

proof.text: First show that $C^\simeq$ is Kan for each $C=F,G,H,J$. The unique map $C\to\Delta^0$ is an isofibration: fill inner horns using the quasicategory condition on $C$, and lift the only equivalence edge in the point by the degenerate identity edge at the specified source vertex. The existing core-fibration lemma therefore makes $C^\simeq\to(\Delta^0)^\simeq=\Delta^0$ a Kan fibration. A horn in $C^\simeq$ has a unique bottom simplex in the point, so its relative filler is exactly a Kan filler in $C^\simeq$. Apply the same lemma to the isofibration $p_Q:H\to G$ from step 2 to obtain a Kan fibration $p_Q^\simeq:H^\simeq\to G^\simeq$. All four quasicategories are small by step 2.

Write $X=F^\simeq\times_{G^\simeq}H^\simeq$ and regard it as a simplicial subset of $J=F\times_G H$. This $X$ is Kan: for a horn in $X$, fill its $F^\simeq$ coordinate first and then lift its $H^\simeq$ coordinate against $p_Q^\simeq$ over the image of that filler in $G^\simeq$. The pair fills the horn in $X$. Both projections from $J$ carry inverse edges and their two triangle witnesses to inverse edges and witnesses. Hence every simplex of $J^\simeq$ lies in $X$. Conversely, apply the final assertion of the existing core-fibration lemma to the Kan complex $X$: every edge of $X$ is an equivalence. The inclusion $X\to J$ preserves the inverse witnesses, so every edge of $X$ becomes an equivalence in $J$. The definition of the core now gives $X\subseteq J^\simeq$. These two inclusions prove the strict identity $J^\simeq=F^\simeq\times_{G^\simeq}H^\simeq$.

source.place: Corollary 4.4.3.19, proof of (2); the Kan-subcomplex argument, with the core inclusion justified explicitly.

proof.text: Apply the existing Kan pullback/path-space comparison to $u:F^\simeq\to G^\simeq$ and $v=p_Q^\simeq:H^\simeq\to G^\simeq$. All three objects are Kan by step 3 and $v$ is a Kan fibration, so it identifies the constant-path map from their strict pullback to $F^\simeq\times^h_{G^\simeq}H^\simeq$ as a weak homotopy equivalence. Through the strict identity of step 4 this is precisely the comparison in the item. The homotopy pullback is the path-space model in the statement, not a pullback of spaces of objects or a pullback of homotopy categories.

source.place: Proposition 3.4.0.7 and Construction 3.4.0.3; applied with the second leg a Kan fibration.

proof.text: The maps just used commute with precomposition in $Q$: on $n$-simplices both projections restrict the two coordinates, while the third coordinate is the constant path at their common composite. Thus for every $Q$ the displayed map is the mapping-space comparison of the given projection square. By the specified mapping spaces $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathrm{Cat}_\infty}(Q,C)=\operatorname{Fun}(Q,C)^\simeq$, the defining universal property of a pullback is exactly that all these comparisons are equivalences of spaces. Step 5 proves this property. Together with step 1 it proves both assertions, without any fibration assumption on $g$.

source.place: Proposition 4.5.3.15 and Remark 4.5.3.16, interpreted as the mapping-space universal property specified in the item.
